claims.claim: Texture can refer to the look and feel of a surface and can be materially present or visually suggested.
In two-dimensional works, color, line, and shading can suggest surface qualities; three-dimensional works can have actual tactile texture.
Artists can produce surface differences through varied tools, mark types, paint buildup, scratching, layering, and materials.
Texture is closely related to material and can be examined in formal visual analysis alongside other visible features.
Pattern is a repeated arrangement, while texture is a surface quality; the two can coexist but should not be treated as synonyms.
Photographs and reproductions can support visible-surface description but have limits for tactile and technical claims about an original object.
